title: The king's five fires
hook: a king asks a proud young scholar five questions he can't answer, and the answer turns out to be the whole cycle of life told as five fires
carry: all of life is an offering

segments.voice: Yesterday: Upakosala, who tended the fires for twelve years. The fires taught him the worlds; his teacher pointed him to the seer in the eye. Your line was the guru points you to the self within.

A young man named Shvetaketu comes to the assembly of the Panchalas, where Pravahana Jaivali is king. The king asks: has your father taught you? Yes, sir. Then do you know where people go when they leave this world? No. How they come back? No. Why that other world never fills up? No. Five questions, five blanks. Shvetaketu goes home, stung: you told me you had taught me! His father admits he doesn't know either. So the father goes to the king himself and asks to be taught. And what the king teaches him is a picture of five fires.
screen: `FIVE QUESTIONS, FIVE BLANKS.` → `THE FATHER DOESN'T KNOW EITHER.` → `HE GOES TO THE KING.`

segments.voice: Go back to the sacrifice from the first day of this year: a fire, and an offering poured into it. The king says the whole world works like that. Five fires, five offerings. The first fire is the sky world up there. The gods pour in faith, and out of it comes Soma, the moon. The second fire is the rain cloud: Soma goes in, and out comes rain. The third is the earth: rain goes in, and out comes food, rice, barley, plants. The fourth is a man: food goes in, and out comes seed. The fifth is a woman: seed goes in, and out comes an embryo, a child on the way. Then the line the whole passage rests on: in the fifth offering, the waters come to be called a person. Rain to food to seed to person. And it doesn't stop at birth. The person lives, dies, and is placed on the funeral fire, the last fire, and the cycle turns again. Notice who's teaching: a king, a warrior, teaching a priest; the text has the king say this knowledge had not gone to brahmins before. And notice the big idea underneath. It's yajna, offering, stretched over the whole of life: not only on the altar, but in clouds, soil, bodies and births. It's why fire still stands at the center of Hindu life. A couple walks around it at their wedding, a family feeds it ghee at a havan, and at the very end, the body itself is given to it.
screen: `THE KING'S FIVE FIRES.` · `SKY, CLOUD, EARTH, MAN, WOMAN.` · `THE WATERS BECOME A PERSON.` · `A KING TEACHES A PRIEST.` · then, large: `ALL OF LIFE IS AN OFFERING.`

segments.voice: Follow the water with your breath. Breathe in and picture rain falling somewhere far away; then a field, a grain of rice, fed by that rain; then a meal that became part of you. Then feel yourself sitting here, made, the king would say, of offered rain.
Pancagni, the five fires: sky, rain cloud, earth, man and woman, each receiving an offering and giving something new, until the waters become a person.
Keep this one: all of life is an offering. Rain to food to seed to person. Tomorrow, that father and son again. Until then.

howItsDone: Hindu rites of passage, from conception to cremation, are traditionally performed around a sacred fire, and cremation is treated in Hindu rites as a final offering into the fire.

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): hook no longer invents Shvetaketu's arrogance or 'storms home' (5.3 sets the scene at the Panchala assembly and has him go home and complain); 'famous teacher' cut; 'Picture the sacrifice you met at the start of the week' fixed (that was day 332, last week); child rendered as embryo; trapdoor's 'one of the oldest accounts of rebirth' cut.
The king's questions are compressed: the script names three of the five (5.3.2–3). Confirm the paraphrase.
In 5.3.7 the king says this knowledge had not gone to brahmins before; the script reports that without commentary. Confirm tone.
Five fires: yonder world (faith → King Soma), Parjanya (Soma → rain), earth (rain → food), man (food → seed), woman (seed → embryo). Confirm 'Soma, the moon' identification.
Shvetaketu's father is Gautama (Uddalaka Aruni), who appears by name tomorrow.
